Halter Overview
About Halter
Halter is a New Zealand-based agtech company producing solar-powered GPS collars for cattle and sheep. The virtual fencing system delivers audio cues and mild pulses to contain livestock within pastures while tracking health metrics and water usage via cloud dashboard. Deployed on over one million animals, Halter serves dairy and beef farmers in Australia and North America.

The platform includes smart collars, connectivity towers, and a mobile app that enables ranchers to manage their cattle using sound and vibration cues, improving grazing efficiency and reducing environmental impact. In June 2025, Halter raised $100 million in Series D funding at a $1 billion valuation, led by global technology investment firm BOND with participation from NewView Capital and continued backing from existing investors Bessemer Venture Partners, DCVC, Blackbird, Icehouse Ventures, and Promus Ventures. The funding validates Halter's focus on physical automation and real-time data solutions for legacy agricultural bottlenecks. At the time of the round, Halter was supporting approximately 150 ranchers across 18 states in the US following its expansion into the American market in the prior year. The capital was allocated to support product development, strengthen US operations, and unlock productivity gains for additional ranchers. Halter addresses significant market tailwinds including aging rancher demographics, severe rural labor shortages, and climate pressures, within a ranching sector generating over $1 trillion annually worldwide. The company has been recognized as New Zealand's fastest-growing company by the Deloitte Fast50 index. |
| Mar 2023 | Series C | Bessemer Venture P…, Promus Ventures +4Bessemer Venture Partners (lead); Promus Ventures; Blackbird Ventures; Icehouse Ventures; Peter Beck; DCVC | $53M  Halter is a New Zealand-based agritech company providing a v…Halter is a New Zealand-based agritech company providing a virtual fencing and animal management system for dairy and beef farms, using solar-powered smart collars, connectivity towers, and a mobile app to enable farmers to manage cattle remotely through sound, vibration cues, rotational grazing, and 24/7 monitoring. The Series C funding round on March 30, 2023, raised $85 million with Bessemer Venture Partners as lead investor, alongside Blackbird Ventures, DCVC, Icehouse Ventures, Peter Beck, and Promus Ventures. This followed prior rounds, bringing total funding to $113.6 million across five rounds as of that date. The company had expanded to the US by early 2023, supporting ranchers across 18 states, amid labor shortages and a focus on productivity gains. Subsequent Series D rounds in 2025 raised $100 million (or equivalently $165M NZD) at a $1 billion USD post-money valuation, led by BOND with participation from NewView Capital and existing investors including Bessemer, DCVC, Blackbird, Icehouse, and Promus, to fuel US expansion and product innovations. Halter was named New Zealand's fastest-growing company by Deloitte Fast50 and positioned its platform as the leading operating system for farms. |

The company has expanded from New Zealand and Australia to the US, supporting around 150 ranchers across 18 states as of recent updates. Blackbird Ventures first invested in Halter in 2021, aligning with the queried round involving DCVC, Peter Beck, Promus Ventures, and Ubiquity Ventures, with Blackbird as lead. Sources confirm Blackbird's involvement in Halter starting April 27, 2021, linked to Series B, with continued participation in later rounds like Series C in 2023 ($85M led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Blackbird, DCVC, Icehouse Ventures, Peter Beck) and Series D in June 2025 ($100M led by BOND, reaching $1B valuation, with NewView, Bessemer, DCVC, Blackbird, Icehouse, Promus). Overall, Halter has raised $213.6M over 7 rounds. Halter achieved exponential growth through a small sales team during COVID-19 restrictions using phone/zoom sales, with ambitions for global scale beyond New Zealand. Blackbird views Halter as a potential default operating system for farms worldwide and one of New Zealand's great companies. The US beef market context highlights cattle products generating over $1 trillion annually, addressing labor, time, and automation bottlenecks in ranching. |

Apeel Sciences
Apeel Sciences is a Santa Barbara-based agtech company producing plant-derived coatings that extend shelf life for avocados, apples, mangos, cucumbers, and citrus fruits. The edible barriers reduce water loss and oxidation, enabling longer supply chains without refrigeration for growers in the United States, Mexico, and Europe.

Genus
Genus PLC is an animal genetics company focused on improving cattle and pig populations to support sustainable food production. The company operates through two main business units: one providing bovine genetics mainly for dairy and beef cattle, and the other offering porcine genetics for pork production. Genus develops genetically superior breeding animals using scientific techniques. It generates revenue by selling genetics, including semen and embryos, as well as through related services under multi-year royalty agreements. The principal activities of each segment are: (a) Genus PIC porcine sales business, (b) Genus ABS: bovine sales business, and (c) Genus Research and Development: spending on research and development.

Distynct
Distynct is an AgTech company delivering precision livestock farming solutions for remote monitoring of swine production facilities. The platform provides real-time data on animal health and facility conditions. Ames-based in Iowa, Distynct targets U.S. pork producers with sensor-based technologies.

Bowery Farming
Bowery Farming is a New York City-based vertical farming company founded in 2015 that operates indoor facilities in New York, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Kentucky. The company grows pesticide-free leafy greens, herbs, strawberries, and microgreens using its proprietary BoweryOS platform, which integrates computer vision, automation, and machine learning for continuous plant monitoring. These farms achieve 95 percent less water usage and over 100 times the productivity per square foot compared to traditional field farming. Bowery produce reaches consumers through Whole Foods Market locations across the Northeast, select Foragers Market stores in the New York area, and menus at Tom Colicchio's Craft and Fowler & Wells restaurants in Manhattan.

Niqo Robotics
Niqo Robotics is a Wageningen-headquartered developer of autonomous agricultural robots equipped with AI-driven computer vision. Its precision sprayers identify and treat weeds selectively, slashing weeding expenses for farmers cultivating row crops like potatoes and sugar beets. The Dutch firm combines robotics hardware with machine learning software to enable efficient, eco-friendly field operations across Europe.

Biobest
Biobest is a Belgium-headquartered supplier of biological crop protection and pollination systems. Based in Westerlo, it offers bumblebees for pollination, beneficial insects and mites like Phytoseiulus persimilis, nematodes, biopesticides, sticky traps, and pheromone lures to growers internationally.

Shiji Biotechnology
Shiji Biotechnology is a Beijing-headquartered developer of genetic technologies for swine breeding. The company engineers pig breeds resistant to diseases like African swine fever using CRISPR gene editing. Shiji offers breeding stock, semen, and consulting services to large-scale farms across China. Established in 2016, it collaborates with the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences on porcine genomics research.

FMC
FMC is a pure-play global crop protection company with a fairly balanced product portfolio across geographies and crop exposure. Through acquisitions, FMC is now one of the five largest patented crop protection companies and focuses on the development of new products, including biologicals, through its research and development pipeline.

eFishery
eFishery is a Jakarta-based aquaculture technology provider founded in 2013 that equips fish and shrimp farmers with smart feeding systems, IoT sensors, and cloud-based analytics platforms. Its eFeeder devices automate feeding schedules across Indonesia, Vietnam, and India, serving more than 100,000 ponds. The company achieved unicorn status in 2023 after raising $137 million in Series D funding from investors including SoftBank. eFishery delivers financing, insurance, and supply chain services through its full-stack ecosystem, enhancing yields by up to 30 percent while minimizing feed waste in Southeast Asia's $20 billion aquaculture market.

ScottsMiracle-Gro
Scotts Miracle-Gro is the largest purveyor of home lawn and gardening products in the US. The company sells a broad range of lawncare products, including grass seed, fertilizer, and lawn-related weed, animal, and disease control. US consumer typically generates the vast majority of companywide revenue and profits. Its lawncare and gardening products are well-recognized brands in the US, including Scotts, Miracle-Gro, Roundup, Ortho, and Tomcat.

CVR Partners
CVR Partners LP is a manufacturer and supplier of nitrogen fertilizer products. Its principal products include Urea Ammonium Nitrate (UAN) and ammonia. The company market ammonia products to industrial and agricultural customers and UAN products to agricultural customers. The primary geographic markets for its fertilizer products are Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, Colorado, and Texas. The company's product sales are heavily weighted toward UAN.

K+S
K+S AG produces two products: fertilizer and salt. The company engaged in business with potash and magnesium products from plants in Germany and Canadian sites in Bethune, as well as the European salt activities. It also includes the waste disposal and recycling business in Germany. extraction and processing of raw materials.

Braiin
Braiin Ltd is an Australian technology company leveraging proprietary intellectual property and patented artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) technologies to deliver actionable insights across the verticals: Agriculture, Property Technology, and Customer Experience as a Service (CXaaS). The company's platforms are designed to address inefficiencies and drive data-backed decision-making across traditionally analog sectors. It prominently focuses on the agriculture technology sector, where it has successfully deployed its AI-powered solutions across multiple implementations. It provides end-to-end solutions to improve farming productivity using IoTs, Wireless Connectivity, Robotics, Software and AI/ML.

Nxin
Nxin is a Beijing-based agricultural technology company that operates a rural financial platform connecting farmers with credit and digital services. It provides supply chain financing, crop insurance, and e-commerce for inputs like seeds and fertilizers via its app serving 10 million users in China. Established in 2013, Nxin partners with Agricultural Bank of China and processes ¥50 billion in annual transactions, promoting IoT sensors for precision farming in provinces including Henan and Shandong.

PI Indus
PI Industries Ltd manufactures, distributes, and sells agrochemicals, specialty fertilizers, and seeds to the agriculture industry. The firm's agrochemicals portfolio includes insecticides, fungicides, and plant health products. The company competes on price with the manufacture and sale of generic products. PI Industries reports sales across two geographical segments: within India and outside India. The outside India division represents its business division predominantly in Japan, Germany, and China. In India, the firm sells its products through a large network of distributors and retail outlets. The company has one reportable business segment which is Agro Chemicals.

Farmers Business Network
Farmers Business Network is a San Carlos-headquartered agricultural technology platform that equips farmers in the United States, Canada, Brazil, and Argentina with data-driven tools for crop management. It offers e-commerce for farm inputs like seeds and fertilizers, agronomic insights from satellite imagery and soil sensors, crop marketing services, and insurance products. The farmer-to-farmer network fosters peer benchmarking on yields and costs. FBN Finance provides direct lending for equipment and inputs, while its marketplace connects producers to buyers for grains and oilseeds.

Infarm
Infarm is a Berlin-headquartered urban farming company deploying modular vertical farms in supermarkets and cities. Founded in 2013, it grows herbs, leafy greens, and strawberries using IoT-controlled hydroponics and machine learning for optimal yields. Infarm partners with chains like Metro and Carrefour, supplying fresh produce in Germany, France, and the United States.

Semios
Semios is a Vancouver-headquartered precision agriculture platform for orchard and vineyard growers. It deploys in-field wireless sensor networks, automated pest monitoring traps, and variable-rate biopesticide sprayers. The system delivers real-time data on crop health, irrigation, and pest pressure via a cloud dashboard. Founded in 2010, Semios serves over 1,000 farms across North America and Chile reducing water use by 20 percent and pesticide applications.

Halter, based in Parnell, Auckland, New Zealand, designs solar-powered, GPS-enabled smart collars for dairy cows and cattle, functioning as an operating system for pasture-based farms by enabling virtual fencing, automated shifting, and real-time health monitoring via a mobile app. The company's system is deployed on over 1,000 farms, with nearly 700,000 collars live globally as of 2025, supported by a team of over 300 employees. Halter achieved unicorn status with a billion-dollar valuation and generated $8.8 million in revenue, having recently secured $100 million in Series D funding in 2025, contributing to 352,939 miles of virtual fencing globally. Lead investors in its funding rounds include BOND, NewView Capital, Blackbird, and DCVC. Founded by Craig Piggott, the company's exact founding year is not publicly known.

Deep Dive
High-Level Overview
Halter is an agricultural technology company that has built a virtual fencing and pasture management platform for dairy farms and beef ranches. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Auckland, New Zealand, Halter develops solar-powered smart collars that enable farmers to manage cattle remotely through a mobile app, replacing traditional physical fencing with digital boundaries. The company serves a critical pain point in modern agriculture: labor shortages, land optimization, and animal welfare management. With over 1,000 farms now using its platform across New Zealand, Australia, and the United States, and a recent $100 million funding round valuing the company at $1 billion, Halter has emerged as the category leader in virtual fencing technology.
The core value proposition centers on three interconnected benefits: increased pasture utilization through rotational grazing, reduced labor demands via automated herd management, and real-time health monitoring of livestock. By combining hardware (collars and transmission towers), software (a mobile app), and connectivity infrastructure, Halter functions as an "operating system" for farm operations rather than a standalone tool.
Origin Story
Halter's founding is deeply rooted in personal experience. Craig Piggott, the company's founder and CEO, grew up on a dairy farm in New Zealand's Waikato district, where he witnessed his parents working 100+ hour weeks managing their herd and land. After studying Mechanical Engineering at the University of Auckland and working as an early engineer at Rocket Lab, Piggott converged his two worlds in 2016 to create Halter.
The breakthrough moment came through a simple but powerful demonstration: Piggott remotely guided a cow named Big Bird to a specific corner of a paddock using only a collar-based system, proving that cattle could be controlled through sound and vibration cues without physical fencing. Early development involved solving unexpected engineering challenges—most notably, finding a solar panel durable enough to withstand the impact equivalent of a golf ball being driven off the tee, ultimately requiring technology similar to bulletproof glass. These early deployments required the entire company to travel to farms for hands-on collar calibration, creating a culture of direct customer engagement that persists today.
Core Differentiators
 Category Leadership at Scale: Halter operates with no meaningful competition in virtual fencing, with competitors "orders of magnitude behind" in both scale and product maturity. The company has deployed over 11,000 miles of virtual fencing across the U.S. alone, representing an estimated $220 million in savings compared to traditional fencing costs.
 Hardware-Software Integration: Unlike software-only solutions, Halter controls the entire stack—solar-powered collars, transmission towers for farm connectivity (requiring no cell coverage), and a user-friendly mobile app. This vertical integration creates a data flywheel that competitors cannot easily replicate.
 Proven Customer Adoption: The platform now operates on over 1,000 farms globally, with more than 200 ranchers across 22 states in the U.S. alone. Customer testimonials and video case studies demonstrate strong product-market fit and user satisfaction.
 Data-Driven Insights: The system provides real-time herd health monitoring, fertility tracking, early illness detection, and precise location data—transforming farms from reactive to proactive management models.
 Founder-Led Engineering Culture: Piggott's background in mechanical engineering and his early experience at Rocket Lab shaped a company culture focused on solving hard technical problems and maintaining direct relationships with farmers.
Role in the Broader Tech Landscape
Halter exemplifies the emerging "software beyond the screen" thesis—technology that extends beyond digital interfaces to physically transform real-world operations. The company is riding several converging trends:
Labor Shortage Crisis: Agriculture faces severe workforce shortages, and Halter's automation directly addresses this by reducing manual herding and monitoring work.
Sustainability Imperatives: Virtual fencing enables rotational grazing practices that improve pasture health, increase milk yields, and reduce environmental impact—aligning with growing ESG pressures on food production.
Precision Agriculture Adoption: The broader agtech sector is moving toward data-driven decision-making, and Halter's real-time monitoring capabilities position it at the forefront of this shift.
Capital Availability for Climate Tech: The $100 million Series D funding round reflects investor confidence in climate-adjacent agricultural solutions, signaling that agtech has matured beyond niche status.
Halter's influence extends beyond its direct customers—the company is legitimizing virtual fencing as a category and demonstrating that even traditional industries can be rewired through thoughtful technology design and deep domain expertise.
Quick Take & Future Outlook
Halter has achieved unicorn status by solving a problem that affects millions of farmers globally: how to manage land and livestock more efficiently with fewer resources. The company's $1 billion valuation reflects not just current traction but the massive addressable market—there are approximately 1 billion cattle globally, and virtual fencing technology is still in early adoption phases outside the U.S., New Zealand, and Australia.
Looking ahead, Halter is developing additional livestock management tools scheduled for 2026, designed to improve automation and accessibility based on user feedback. The company's expansion trajectory suggests it will likely pursue international markets in Europe and South America, where labor costs and land constraints create similar pressures to those in its current markets.
The deeper significance of Halter's rise is that it proves venture-backed technology can create category-defining companies in industries that seem resistant to disruption. By combining founder empathy, engineering rigor, and boots-on-the-ground customer engagement, Halter has built a defensible moat that extends far beyond software—it's embedded in the daily operations of modern farms.
